chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Playing for wounded soldiers at Walter Reed
summary: McRae calls the hospital show one of the hardest dates of his life, as hundreds of amputees lined the aisle.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: We did the hospital in Washington, D.C. -- that big hospital down there.
Walter Reed, yeah. That was one of the hardest dates I ever played in my life.
When we walked in there -- I wanna tell you this. When we walked in there, they had all these soldiers, and lot of them had lost their limbs and legs, and everything.
The bandstand was all the way down front. We had to walk down an aisle, and they were on both sides of us. Just hundreds of them, you know.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And they just come back (inaudible) from overseas. I think -- Velma and I almost fell out. She couldn't -- well, she got weak going down there.
Yeah, it really gets to you, you know, but (inaudible) all those different things and seeing all those different people come back from the Army.
I enjoyed it. It was a part (inaudible) we had to do. That's the only way we could get around like that.
